reviews.comment: I am so late to the game on my review. NGL, most of the reviews you are reading are true but exaggerated. At first I did not do well on my first test, but I read the textbook, and it helped tremendously! Overall, you totally got this if you study; don't listen to the bad stuff ( and that is coming from someone who has to work hard to understand)

Genuinely the worst class I have ever had. Yes I am back four months after I took his class to write this just because of how bad it was. Stopped attendance after a month, I went to class all semester, went to SI sessions, prayed, cried a lot just to get my A, and it was not by the grace of Michael. Be prepared to teach yourself and good luck..

If I were on my deathbed and only had 7 minutes to live I would choose one of his lectures so it could feel like an eternity. I do believe he is a good person and hilarious at that, but as a professor no. He has exams that are way more difficult than any other Chem proffesor. But if passing is possible, if you watch YT and go to SI instead.

If you took AP Chem, this class/exams should be easy enough regardless of the prof's shortcomings. If not, stay away from Nippe. He mumbles through ppt slides and doesn't answer questions well. There's no point of going to lecture, as he reads straight off of ppts which get posted to Canvas, and he provides no additional insight during class.

he mumbles into the microphone, you cannot hear a word he is saying. he is passive aggressive and dodges questions, such as when students ask a question he will not elaborate or will simply not answer. though his practice exams were similar to the actual exams, the final was ridiculous and nothing like the homework or practice.

Do not take him unless you have taken AP Chemistry prior to this class. I would not recommended if gen chem is. completely new to you. Lecture isnt really useful because you cant really understand him when he talks. The weekly quizzes are on canvas with two attempts which is nice. The class is solely reliant on your exam scores so be prepared.

I went early on to his office hours and he ridiculed me for not understanding the topics. Tests were difficult. Lots of extra studying outside of class, a 70 was lucky. If you have previous experience with chemistry, you should be fine. The aleks homework would sometimes take 6 hrs. Professor didn't make the tests or post the homework, the IA did.

Do not listen to the bad reviews. He is funny and his lectures are good if you put in the work to actually listen. He stops mandatory iClicker after like the fourth week. Tests are pretty easy, I think I finished test 3 in 16 minutes and got an A. By far easier than AP Chem. Everyone saying this class is hard probably also stopped going to class.

I would make sure you're prepared to teach yourself. I got nothing out of his lectures, so I'd have to learn everything on my own. His final also felt pretty harsh to me compared to questions other sections of Chem 119 had. I will say this structure of class does force you to learn a lot more in depth, so you will probably be ahead going into 120.

He provides limited practice material and offers little support outside of lecture to help students succeed. While this isn't necessarily his fault, his strong German accent can make lectures difficult to follow at times. Additionally, when students ask questions he doesn't seem to prefer, his responses can come across as dismissive or impatient.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I liked the professor but I learned nothing from lectures. For the 1st month, he assigned about 2 hours of homework every week. The TA was made the tests and grading (which took 3 weeks to get back a scantron). I would never choose to take this class again. The only reason I managed to get through it was thanks to the excellent SI instructor.

This class is very easy. People say Nippe just reads off slides, but I think theyre just not paying attention in class. He explains the 'why' behind topics, which made me understand chem way better. Attendance stops being mandatory after a few weeks. His tests are literally easier than high school chem sometimes. Recommend if you like chemistry.

He doesn't teach at all whatsoever. He scribbles on the board and then just says that he doesn't feel like going over something, or that we should already know it even though this is gen chem. He didn't put any of the grades he said he would or drop a low exam as stated in the syllabus. Please for your own sanity do not take him. Worst class ever.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is possible to do good in this class but not because of the professor at all. I left all the lectures more confused than before even if I've studied the material beforehand because what he was talking about made no sense. complete self study class but if you use your resources and OCHEM tutor on youtube its not too bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's not impossible to get an A in the class, but the only reason I managed to do it was by teaching myself everything. USE THE ALEKS TEXTBOOK! Every single problem in his lectures is from the textbook. Go to SI sessions. Dr. Nippe is a kind man, but he goes off on tangents about advanced chem and doesn't spend enough time on the actual curriculum.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My first red flag came the first week of class when everyone was panicking to switch professors. Because I had always been a straight A student I decided to give him a chance which turned out to be a mistake as I ended with a C. He reads straight off the slides which are hard to follow and gives little help for tests which are difficult.

I don't think you could have a prof worse than him. He seems like a fun guy, but he is really bad at teaching, gives a ton of homework which doesn't align with the tests, and no extra credit. For exams, we also get as little info as possible (periodic table and that's basically it). Exam means were around 60-70%. Trust, I had to STRUGGLE for an A.

Great guy but I think if you chose a random student that has taken the course they could teach better than him. Everyone learned more at the SI sessions than the actual lectures, and he is the only chem professor that doesn't give you anything besides the periodic table and a couple of random equations you don't even need on the formula sheet.

He gave about 6 homework assignments a week, but all of that hard work was only 6% of the class grade. He never responded to my emails. His office hours location led me on a treasure hunt. Turns out his “drop by any time” mean he does not even have then in person (different from syllabus). Test are multiple choice but never in the style practiced.

Do NOT take this professor!! It genuinely crumbled my mental health to the point where I am having to seek outside help for this class alone! He reads off the slides with his accent. He is funny I will give him that, but your grade will be even funnier. TA does all the work. Did not even communicate our final was on a different day than syllabus.

You can totally survive his class. Quizzes are online not in lock down. In lecture, he only reads slides. The content is good but impossible if you like to take notes. Exams are very straight forward and have minimal tricks, but they are 20 question MC. Do his practice problems and watch youtube videos. A+ tutoring didn't help me with this course.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: okay hes not a bad professor he justs reads off slides the entire class, other than that his class isnt so bad but you would have to study ever single day after to know the material well for the exams.

You basically teach yourself the whole semester, and you have no clue what to expect on the exams. The professor does not care about you or the class, and the TA does all the work making quizzes, exams, and homework. There is a huge disconnect between the SI sessions and the actual exam. he doesnt curve any exams or give extra credit.

I do not recommend this professor. He will make you memorize everything (solubility charts, electronegativity, etc.). This is extremely different from other professors provide students with such information on their exams. In class, he just reads of the slides and does not work out any of the problems (simply reads the steps & answer).
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM! He would read off the slide and had an attitude. I basically paid the UNI to get a professor to read off the textbook. He doesn't even make his own exams or give reviews; his TA does it all. TBH, just use Spartan tutoring or A+ tutoring, Organic chemist tutor on YT, and maybe you will be good. The lab is worth 25% of the grade

Worst gen chem professor. Reads directly off the slides but can't explain how to get to the answer. Homework was LONG and TEDIOUS. Test heavy, that's your entire grade. Provides no resources to help you out. Paying for nothing basically.

Lectures are unproductive and boring. Homework and quizzes are super unpredictable. Just overall not great, but I survived with an A, and at the end of the day, it really just matters how well you can comprehend the material by yourself.

This class was my own personal hell. Professor Nippe is not a great lecturer and I often find him mumbling throughout the class. He is extremely difficult to follow and did not explain the concepts well AT ALL. I had to learn most if not all of the coursework on my own time outside of class. If you have any say in it, TAKE ANYBODY ELSE.

I attended every lecture but had difficulty following his explanations. He encourages you to ask questions if something does not make sense. Attendance was mandatory at first. Exams are fairly easy, but I didn't study for the first which is the reason for my grade. I wouldn't recommend taking his class if you can't make an effort to self-study.

He reads off the slides and you can never hear him unless you're sitting in the front row and even then he makes no sense. I had to teach myself everything, I even stopped going to his lectures because they don't help at all. I would not recommend taking him if you don't like teaching yourself.

He isn't a horrible prof, he really just reads off the powerpoint and expects people to know the concepts he teaches, would not recommend if you didn't take a chemistry college course before. When you listen to him and really pay attention you do understand what he teaches however, he does not teach what is on the exam.

He is absolutely terrible. He only teaches once every 2 years, SI sessions will carry your grade. For tests he says he gives stuff but then he removes it last minute like solubility charts, electronegativity chart, etc. If you have to take him best of luck. The tests aren't the worst but he just doesn't teach, so I guess thats the trade off.

I've tried so hard to apply myself in this class but it is incredibly difficult to follow along with his lectures. He expects you to know exactly what he's talking about at all times, even if he's confused himself. Offers no extra help or extra credit besides SI sessions run by the awesome TA.

Would never take again. Doesn't seem to care about how we do in the class and is very M.I.A. Outside of the actual class time. He doesn't offer extra credit and he just reads off the slides. Doesn't explain steps well and his accent is hard to understand.

I had Dr. Nippe for CHEM 483. He is genuinely the funniest professor I've had. If you can memorize the equations from the first half of the course, you'll be fine. I took the class as a sophomore and didn't find it to be too difficult. I highly recommend asking questions after class if you are confused or interested in a concept.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful Professor! I was looking forward to taking his class for several months, only to be seriously disappointed by the teacher. Made class stressful and I felt uncomfortable to ask questions or seek help. He has that attitude of either you know it or figure it out yourself. Just be prepared y'all.

Loved inorg lab! Super friendly & a literal comedian. Oral prelabs weren't that bad, but lab reports are graded pretty harshly by TAs. Make sure to read and APPLY all report comments for future reports. Started with like a 70 on the first one and got a 97 on the last by just applying their edits. By far my favorite chem lab in undergrad.

Nippe was a cliche powerpoint professor with illegible handwriting. He would only use powerpoint presentations, which would often have information that was useless or was just poorly explained. When I tried to ask him questions on topics, he would just tell me an answer that didn't help or just tell me not to worry about it. Recommend SI Sessions.

Dr. Nippe was a boring professor. He was kinda funny, but monotone and read off slides. He took attendance but stopped halfway through the semester, so I stopped going to lectures. Few homework assignments that are easy to do. Exams are relatively easy, especially compared to other professors. I barely studied for the exams, which is why I got a B.

most people who took him for chem119 could probably tell right away that this professor was probably there for research. has no intention of actually teaching the material or allowing questions but rather is more interested in reading off the slides. skipped a month of lectures cause it was unbearable, used ALEKS, and still got an A in the course
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had to work really hard and attend outside tutoring. He is a sweet guy, but you have to put in outside work to succeed. I felt lost in lectures because he talks about high level chemistry. If you take him, be prepared to put in the work! Do all the homework, attend class for iClicker, and get all the points you can in lab!

DO NOT TAKE. If you care about yourself, do not take. He does seem sweet honestly. Difficult to understand lectures, self-taught material. A lot of homework that is not posted on Canvas, watch out. Easy enough quizzes, humbling tests that get harder. I was genuinely failing for most of the semester but got to a B somehow so its possible y'all.

Professor Nippe himself did not do the best job at teaching, however if you have prior chemistry background, this class is an easy A. All of his tests are super easy, quizzes are all online, and homework (ALEKS) will prepare you well for the math portion of the exams. Recommend taking him if you already know what you are doing!

His tests are known to be difficult -- so I am not sure why people think that they are easy. Most people agree with this. He's funny, his accent is not super bad but it's strong. I don't think he handles his grades so he does not really know what to teach us. Quizzes are easy and grade booster, but tests and aleks will tank you if you let it.

Dr. Nippe is the coolest professor I have had so far, but it is clear that he does not have enough time on his hands to teach this class. He does not handle the tests, the homework, the quizzes, and I am not completely sure he really knows what will be on them. This will be a complete self learn class with the upside of a stand up comedian in lec.

Nippe is a funny guy but I lose my attention span within 15 mins of his lectures. He skips over worked examples because we can "look at them outside of class" and does not share any reviews or practice exams. I only learned Chemsitry through my SI so get ready for a lot of self-teaching.
Very lecture heavy, leaves a lot of homework that WILL drop your grade if not done. He is not aware of anything that is on the exam as well. Overall, you would have to teach yourself.

Nippe himself was ok, expect lots of self teaching. His lecture notes were amazing and really helped me understand. SI good. His tests were very simple. crammed last min and got an A on 2/3 exams. (don't recommend that tho) However make sure you do the ALEKS hw. It was so tedious but I missed a lot and my grade dropped a lot. Quizzes ez too (95%+)
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you do not have prior chem knowledge or do not want to read/work outside of class, I would not take this professor. He is funny, but does not fully know how to explain concepts to a gen chem class. I liked his enthusiasm and I enjoyed learning through his lectures, but I had lots of chem experience before this class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! I have already taken AP chem and did well but I do not understand him or what he teaches. Please do not take him, you will end up teaching yourself. Also the homework does not relate to what we learn. Also he seems confused on what is on the exams and will tell his class different things than he tells the SI.

Absolutely terrible. He completely disregards the syllabus (he copied it off of another prof). He will go through topics thoroughly just to tell us that we will be not be tested on them and then does not teach the things the exams are actually on. Be prepared for having to teach yourself entirely and not be offered any grace or extra credit.

Nippe is a great freshman chem professor. He makes his lectures entertaining and explains concepts multiple ways. We used clicker points in class until the system broke so attendance is up to the student. Aleks for homework and bonus on every exam.

This professor seems like a very nice person, but his sense of humor is very dry and puts some people off. He's very intelligent and therefore has the tendency to overcomplicate or over explain things. Also, if you can't understand accents, don't take him. Very thick German accent. Had to drop the class from a lack of understanding.

Very hard to understand. He is not good at teaching or explaining things. I mostly teach myself. There is a lot of homework and a lot of times it does not relate to what we are learning in class. Tests are hard (though mostly multiple choice) and there are a lot of quizzes that he forgets to tell us about. Also the homework is usually difficult.

Dr Nippe is an amazing guy. This is the funniest professor ever, he's actually a part time comedian. His tests are crazy difficult, but he gives you the material to be prepared, and he added a lot of points to his test to add an automatic curve. He loves his kids... and he's not the best lecturer but he wants very badly for you to succeed.

He is a new professor and it shows. He made me feel extremely stupid when asking questions and was not easily accessible outside of class. He is extremely unorganized and taught as if we were graduate students. Unless you are trying to join his research studies or want to become a chemist I would not recommend for anyone.

His class is very hard and he may not be the best professor by the strictest definition of the word, but he truly does care and want you to succeed. He treated even my dumbest questions with respect. You'll need outside help to survive the exams, but he is very good about explaining the "why" behind topics instead of just spewing info at you.
He's really good at chemistry and really wants you to pass but his lectures are really confusing. I watched a lot of Khan Academy to supplement his lectures

Honestly hes not a great professor. He goes on really long tangents that dont relate to anything. If you are not already pretty strong in chemistry dont take him. You have to teach yourself a lot of the material and hes no help at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was new at teaching and it was very obvious. He has a witty personality which made class quicker, plus he let out early most days. The tests are tricky and focuses on concepts over math. He curved a ton because nobody ever knew what was going on and the tests weren't a fair representation of what you were capable of doing.

Nippe is a funny and easy-going guy but he's just not a great teacher. His lectures are very unorganized and he doesn't explain the math very well. The tests are unnecessarily difficult so he ended up giving a massive bell curve on each test. You're gonna need to learn how to teach yourself the material.

Dr. Nippe is a great prof. He knows a lot about chem, and so he goes kinda fast in lecture. He can be a little confusing, but he is very willing to help you if you go to office hours. So seriously, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!  I went and did well on exams. He genuinely wants students to learn the material and do well. I would definitely take him again.

He is hard to understand sometimes because he gets a little confused himself, but overall he is fair. His questions come from the homework he assigns and his lectures nothing random, plus he gives the option of dropping the lowest test which is nice.

Dr. Nippe is a really nice guy, and I'll admit he's pretty funny at times. but when it comes to explaining concepts and lectures, it can be very confusing. He often got lost and just has trouble teaching certain things. He's always willing to answer questions and help though, but most of the things I taught myself through online homework.
Don't take him!!! Whatever you do!!!  He goes on long tangents over things that aren't even on the test... Save yourself some time and don't take him.
